text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egyptian diplomatic measures to push the peace process back in its natural track, cease settlements and protect the status of Jerusalem. Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says after meeting Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak: Contacts are continuous between Mubarak and U.S. President Bill Clinton to save the peace process. Washington has an important role as an impartial mediator.
- Mubarak reviews the budget with Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri, the minister begins an Asian tour during which he will sign 14 treaties.
- Cabinet approves 39 new investment projects with a total capital worth of 1.4 billion pounds ($410 billion)

- Finance Minister Mohieddin el-Gharib says that 1997/8 budget will total 84 billion pounds, compared to 77.5 billion in the previous financial year. Gharib also said after meeting the prime minister that taxes will make up 17 percent of this year's budget compared to 18 percent in the previous year.

- Mubarak reviews the budget with Ganzouri. Investments will total 58 billion in the first year of the five-year plan. Growth rates are forecast at 6.2 percent and the budget deficit at one percent. No new taxes or tariffs in 1997/8.
- The president reviews diplomatic measures to protect the peace process.
- Total investments for the new five-year plan forecast at 400 billion pounds, cabinet says.
- High-level contacts between Mubarak and Clinton to save the peace process.
- New five-year plan will provide 450,000 job opportunities and the state will continue hiring recent graduates.
